items.markingKey: B1 restricted total 32; B1 7/32 [2]

items.stem: Aisha solves 5(5x + 9) = 145. Aisha writes 25x + 9 = 145, so x = 136/25. Explain the error and find the correct value of x.
items.answer: The 9 inside the bracket must also be multiplied by 5: 25x + 45 = 145, so x = 4.
items.markingKey: B1 expands bracket fully; M1 25x = 100; A1 x = 4 [3]

items.stem: Complete the table of values for y = x² + 2x + 5. x = −3: y = ?, x = −2: y = 5, x = −1: y = ?, x = 0: y = ?, x = 1: y = 8, x = 2: y = 13, x = 3: y = 20.
items.markingKey: B1 for each correct missing value [3]

items.stem: Sipho says that a right prism whose cross-section is a regular polygon with 4 sides has 4 planes of symmetry, the same as the number of lines of symmetry of the cross-section. Explain why Sipho is not quite right.
items.answer: There are 4 vertical planes through the lines of symmetry of the cross-section, plus one more plane halfway along the prism parallel to the ends, so 5 planes.
items.markingKey: B1 4 planes from the cross-section; B1 extra plane through the middle, total 5 [2]

items.stem: Use substitution to solve y = 5x + 4 and 5x − 3y = −62.
A camera costs €60.00 in Accra and ¥8,775.00 in Lima. The exchange rate is 1 euro = ¥162.50. Find where it is cheaper and by how much, in euros.
items.markingKey: M1 8775 ÷ 162.5 = €54.00; A1 comparison and difference €6.00.

items.stem: From a cumulative frequency curve, the lowest value is 11, the lower quartile is 21, the upper quartile is 45 and the highest value is 75. Sofia says the interquartile range is 75 − 11 = 64. Explain the error and find the correct interquartile range.
items.answer: Sofia has found the range. IQR = upper quartile − lower quartile = 45 − 21 = 24.
items.markingKey: B1 range vs IQR; B1 24 [2]

items.stem: Triangle XYZ has XY = 14 cm, XZ = 13 cm and angle YXZ = 26°. Calculate the area of the triangle.
In a sale, a tablet costs £272.00 after a 15% discount. Sipho finds the original price by adding 15% of £272.00 and gets £312.80. Explain why this is wrong and find the original price.
items.answer: The discount was 15% of the original price, not of the sale price. Sale price = 85% of original, so original = 272 ÷ 0.85 = £320.00.
items.markingKey: B1 percentage of the wrong amount; M1 ÷ 0.85; A1 £320.00 [3]

items.stem: A supermarket in Mumbai sells washing liquid in these sizes: 330 ml for $0.85, 2000 ml for $4.20, 1500 ml for $3.30. Showing your working, find which size is the best buy.
items.markingKey: M1 cost per litre (or ml per $) for each: 330 ml → $2.576/litre, 2000 ml → $2.100/litre, 1500 ml → $2.200/litre; A1 2000 ml.

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) Explain why ff⁻¹(x) = x for any function f that has an inverse. (b) Explain why f(x) = x² for all real x does not have an inverse function.
items.answer: (a) f⁻¹ reverses the effect of f, so applying f after f⁻¹ returns the original input. (b) Two different inputs (e.g. 3 and −3) give the same output 9, so the inverse would not give a single value.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 inverse undoes; B1 returns x [2] (b) B1 many-to-one; B1 inverse not unique [2]

items.stem: Find the coordinates of the points where the line y = 3x + 3 meets the curve y = x² + 10x + 15.
items.markingKey: M1 x² + 10x + 15 = 3x + 3; M1 x² + 7x + 12 = 0; M1 factorise; A1 x-values; A1 y-values.

items.stem: A, B and C lie on a circle with centre O. Angle AOB = 94°. Sipho says angle ACB = 94° because "they stand on the same arc". Explain the error and give the correct angle.
items.answer: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference, so angle ACB = 47°.
items.markingKey: B1 correct theorem; B1 47° [2]

items.stem: Solve the inequality (3x + 2) / 4 ≥ 2x − 4.
items.markingKey: M1 multiply by 4: 3x + 2 ≥ 8x − 16; M1 −5x ≥ −18; A1 x ≤ 18/5 (sign reversed when dividing by a negative).

items.stem: A lighthouse on the coast near Mexico City has its light 120 m above sea level. From the light, the angles of depression of two boats P and Q, which are in a straight line with the foot of the lighthouse, are 42° and 31°. (a) Calculate the distance of Q from the foot of the lighthouse. (b) Calculate the distance between the two boats. (c) Calculate the straight-line distance from boat P to the light.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 120 ÷ tan 31°; A1 200 [2] (b) M1 subtracts distances; A1 66.4 m [2] (c) M1 120 ÷ sin 42°; A1 [2]

items.markingKey: B1 B1 B1 (one per value); watch signs when cubing negatives.

items.stem: Lucas cycles 15 km at an average speed of x km/h and then 45 km at an average speed of (x + 5) km/h. The total time taken is 4.5 hours. (a) Show that x satisfies the equation 3x² − 25x − 50 = 0. (b) Solve the equation and find the speed for the first part of the journey. (c) Calculate the time taken for the second part of the journey, in hours and minutes.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 multiply by x(x + 5); M1 expand and collect; A1 correct equation [3] (b) M1 factorise/formula; A1 x = 10; B1 rejects x = −5/3 (negative) [3] (c) M1 45 ÷ 15; A1 3 h [2]

items.stem: Isla runs 200 m, measured correct to the nearest metre, in a time of 23.7 s, correct to 1 decimal place, at a school athletics event in Accra. (a) Calculate the upper bound of the average speed. (b) Calculate the lower bound of the average speed. (c) Using your bounds, write down the average speed to an appropriate degree of accuracy, giving a reason.
items.answer: (a) 8.48 m/s (b) 8.40 m/s (c) 8 m/s (1 s.f.), since both bounds round to this

items.stem: The waiting time at a clinic for 151 cases in Kathmandu is summarised as 50 < w ≤ 60: 40; 60 < w ≤ 65: 10; 65 < w ≤ 70: 3; 70 < w ≤ 80: 8; 80 < w ≤ 110: 90 (w in minutes). (a) Write down the points that should be plotted to draw the cumulative frequency curve. (b) Treating the curve as straight between plotted points, estimate the median. (c) Explain why the median from a cumulative frequency curve is an estimate.
items.answer: (a) (50, 0), (60, 40), (65, 50), (70, 53), (80, 61), (110, 151) (b) 84.8 minutes (c) The data are grouped, so the exact values are unknown; values are assumed to be spread through each class.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 upper boundaries; B1 start point [2] (b) M1 CF = 75.5; M1 interpolation within class; A1 [3] (c) B1 [1]

items.stem: A cuboid ABCDEFGH has a rectangular base ABCD with AB = 12 cm and BC = 9 cm, and vertical edges of 5 cm (G is above C). Calculate the angle between the diagonal AG and the base ABCD.

Aisha has €4,000.00 to invest in Singapore. Bank A offers 4% per year simple interest. Bank B offers 3.4% per year compound interest. (a) Calculate the total value with Bank A after 4 years. (b) State which bank gives more after 4 years and by how much. (c) Find the least number of complete years after which Bank B is worth more than Bank A. (d) Explain why Bank B eventually overtakes Bank A even though its rate is lower.
items.answer: (a) €4,640.00 (b) Bank A (simple), by €67.62 (c) 11 years (d) Compound interest grows exponentially (interest on interest) while simple interest grows by a fixed amount each year.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 4000 × 4 × 4/100; A1 €4,640.00 [2] (b) B1 B1 [2] (c) M1 compares values year by year; A1 [3] (d) B1 [1]

items.stem: Zara records the distance from the city centre (km) and the monthly rent ($) for a project in Jakarta. Distance from the city centre (km): 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 14, 15, 16, 17. Monthly rent ($): 1155, 1145, 1807, 1084, 1008, 1002, 770, 728, 684, 661. (a) Identify the outlier and suggest one reason why it might have occurred. (b) Ignoring the outlier, calculate the mean of each variable. (c) A line of best fit, drawn through the mean point and ignoring the outlier, has gradient −45.0. Use it to estimate the monthly rent ($) when the distance from the city centre (km) is 13.
items.answer: (a) (7, 1807); e.g. a recording error or an unusual day/person. (b) (11.11, 915.22) (c) 830 (accept a sensible value close to this)
items.markingKey: (a) B1 point; B1 sensible reason [2] (b) M1 sums ÷ number of values; A1 both [2] (c) M1 y − 915.22 = −45.0(x − 11.11); A1 830 [2]

items.stem: A cuboid block of metal measuring 15 cm by 6 cm by 4 cm has density 8.9 g/cm³. Take the weight of 1 kg to be 10 N. (a) Calculate the mass of the block in kg. (b) Calculate the greatest pressure the block can exert on a table, in N/m².
items.markingKey: (a) M1 V = 360 cm³; M1 × 8.9; A1 [3] (b) M1 smallest face 24 cm² = 0.0024 m²; M1 W ÷ area; A1 [3]

A = {members of a sports club who play football}, B = {members of a sports club who play basketball}. (a) Find the number who do both and complete a Venn diagram. (b) Given that a person is in B, find the probability that they are also in A.
f(x) = 2x and g(x) = 2x − 4. Find fg(x) and gf(x) in their simplest forms.

A curve has equation y = −x³ − 3x² − 8x − 5. The point P on the curve has x-coordinate 2. (a) Find dy/dx. (b) Find the y-coordinate of P. (c) Find dy/dx when x = 3 and state whether the curve is increasing or decreasing there.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 B1 B1 (one per term) [3] (b) B1 [1] (c) M1 A1 [2]

items.stem: Tangents PA and PB are drawn from a point P to a circle with centre O and radius 10 cm. OP = 26 cm. (a) Write down the size of angle OAP, giving a reason. (b) Calculate the length PA. (c) Calculate angle APB. (d) Explain why OP is a line of symmetry of OAPB.
items.answer: (a) 90°: a tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact. (b) 24.0 cm (c) 45.2° (d) Triangles OAP and OBP are congruent (RHS), so reflecting in OP maps A to B.
